stem: A continuous, closed path along which electric current flows is called an __________.
solution: An electric circuit is a complete closed path through which current flows.

stem: The source of electrical energy in a simple circuit is the __________.
solution: A cell or battery provides the electrical energy that drives current in a circuit.

stem: Two or more cells joined together form a __________.
solution: A combination of two or more cells is called a battery.

stem: The device used to open or close a circuit is a __________.
solution: A switch makes or breaks the circuit, turning current on or off.

stem: A bulb glows only when the switch is __________.
solution: A bulb glows only when the switch is on and the circuit is complete.

stem: The thin wire inside a bulb that glows when current passes is the __________.
solution: The filament of a bulb glows and gives light when current flows through it.

stem: A circuit with a complete, unbroken path is called a __________ circuit.
solution: A closed circuit has a complete path, allowing current to flow.

stem: If the wire is broken or the switch is off, the circuit is __________ and no current flows.
solution: An open circuit has a gap, so no current flows and the bulb does not glow.

stem: Materials that allow electric current to pass through them are called __________.
solution: Conductors, like metals, allow electric current to flow through them.

stem: Materials that do not allow electric current to pass through them are called __________.
solution: Insulators, like plastic and rubber, do not allow current to flow.

stem: Which of the following is a good conductor of electricity?
solution: Copper is a good conductor; rubber, plastic and wood are insulators.

stem: Which of the following is an insulator?
solution: Plastic is an insulator; copper, iron and aluminium are conductors.

stem: Electrical wires are covered with plastic or rubber because these materials are __________.
options: insulators that protect us from shocks
solution: Plastic/rubber insulation prevents current from reaching us, protecting against electric shocks.

stem: In a circuit diagram, a cell is represented by __________.
options: a long line and a short line
solution: A cell is shown by a long line (positive terminal) and a short line (negative terminal).

stem: The terminals of a cell are the __________.
solution: A cell has a positive terminal (+) and a negative terminal (−).

stem: In a torch, cells are usually connected in __________.
options: series (positive of one to negative of the next)
solution: Cells in a torch are joined in series, positive to negative, to add their voltages.

stem: A battery gives more energy than a single cell because it __________.
options: combines the voltage of several cells
solution: Combining cells into a battery increases the total voltage and energy available.

stem: The bulb in a circuit gives light because the current produces the __________ effect.
solution: Current heats the filament until it glows, giving light — the heating effect of current.

stem: Which of the following will make a bulb NOT glow in a circuit?
solution: A break in the wire opens the circuit, so no current flows and the bulb does not glow.

stem: A fuse is a safety device that __________ if too much current flows.
solution: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit during overload, protecting appliances.

stem: We should never touch electrical appliances with wet hands because __________.
options: water conducts electricity and can cause a shock
solution: Wet skin and water conduct electricity, increasing the risk of a dangerous shock.

stem: Which of the following components is used to store and supply electrical energy?
solution: A cell stores chemical energy and supplies electrical energy to the circuit.

stem: A simple tester (with a cell and a bulb) can be used to check whether a material is a __________.
solution: If the bulb glows when the material completes the circuit, the material is a conductor; if not, an insulator.

stem: The current in a simple circuit flows from the __________ terminal of the cell through the circuit to the __________ terminal.
solution: Conventional current flows from the positive terminal, through the circuit, back to the negative terminal.

stem: Which of the following is a conductor found in the human body's context (a warning)?
options: The human body (due to body fluids)
solution: The human body conducts electricity (due to its fluids), which is why electric shocks are dangerous.

stem: An LED (light-emitting diode) can be used instead of a bulb because it __________.
options: glows even with a small current and uses less energy
solution: LEDs glow with small currents and are energy-efficient, useful for testing and lighting.

stem: A circuit component that provides resistance and can control current is a __________.
solution: A resistor opposes the flow of current and can be used to control it in a circuit.

stem: When the switch of a torch is pressed, the circuit becomes __________ and the bulb lights up.
solution: Pressing the switch closes (completes) the circuit, allowing current to flow and the bulb to light.

stem: Which of the following correctly lists components of a simple electric circuit?
solution: A simple electric circuit has a cell, connecting wires, a switch and a device like a bulb.

stem: If a bulb is fused (its filament is broken), it will __________ even in a complete circuit.
solution: A fused bulb has a broken filament, so no current can flow through it and it will not glow.

stem: The main safety reason for using an insulated handle on a screwdriver used with electricity is that __________.
options: the insulation prevents current from reaching the hand
solution: The insulating handle stops current from passing to the user, preventing shocks.

stem: Two bulbs connected so that the same current passes through both are connected in __________.
solution: In a series connection, the same current passes through each component one after another.

stem: In a series circuit of two bulbs, if one bulb fuses, the other bulb __________.
solution: In a series circuit, a break in one bulb opens the whole circuit, so the other bulb also stops glowing.

stem: Which household material would be safe to hold while handling a live wire (in principle)?
options: A dry rubber or plastic insulator
solution: Dry insulating materials like rubber or plastic do not conduct electricity, making them safer.

stem: A cell converts __________ energy into electrical energy.
solution: A cell converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy.

stem: The purpose of the switch in a household circuit is to __________.
options: control the flow of current to an appliance
solution: A switch controls whether current flows to an appliance by opening or closing the circuit.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a conductor of electricity?
solution: Glass is an insulator; iron, copper and aluminium are conductors.

stem: The direction of current is taken as the direction in which __________ charge flows.
solution: Conventional current is taken as the direction of flow of positive charge.

stem: A short circuit occurs when __________.
options: the two wires touch directly, allowing a very large current
solution: A short circuit is a direct low-resistance path that causes a dangerously large current to flow.

stem: Which effect of electric current is used in an electric heater?
solution: An electric heater uses the heating effect of current in its element.

stem: In a circuit, wires are used to __________.
options: connect the components and carry the current
solution: Connecting wires join the components and provide a path for the current.

stem: Which of the following would you use to test if a circuit is complete?
options: Measure the temperature of the switch
Look at the colour of the cell
solution: If the bulb glows, the circuit is complete; if not, there is a break somewhere.

stem: A cell that has run down (discharged) will cause the bulb to __________.
solution: A discharged cell supplies little or no energy, so the bulb glows dimly or not at all.

stem: The safest action if an electrical appliance sparks or smells of burning is to __________.
options: switch off the mains and inform an adult
solution: Switch off the power and get help; never pour water on electrical items or touch live wires.

stem: The bulb and the cell in a circuit are connected using __________.
solution: Conducting wires connect the bulb and cell to allow current to flow.

stem: An electric circuit will not work if any component in a series path is __________.
solution: In a series path, a single disconnection or break stops the current everywhere.

stem: Which of the following is used as the filament of a bulb because of its high melting point?
solution: Tungsten is used for bulb filaments due to its very high melting point.

stem: Why should electrical repairs be done by trained people?
options: Electricity can be dangerous and cause shocks or fires if handled wrongly
It is a legal formality only
solution: Electricity can cause serious shocks and fires, so repairs should be done safely by trained people.

stem: A cell has two terminals: the longer line represents the __________ terminal.
solution: In a cell, the longer terminal (line) is the positive terminal and the shorter one is negative.

stem: A device that automatically breaks the circuit when the current becomes dangerously high is a __________.
solution: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit during excessive current, protecting the circuit and preventing fire.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Electricity: Circuits and their Components' is that:
options: electric current flows in a closed circuit made of a cell, wires, switch and devices; materials are conductors or insulators; and electricity must be used safely
solution: The chapter explains electric circuits and their components, conductors and insulators, and the safe use of electricity.
